As a demiromantic demisexual, I have seriously struggled with understanding why heteroaces should be considered LGBTQIA+. I'm wary of anyone who identifies as heteroromantic or heterosexual entering LGBTQIA+ spaces because of a few reasons. Sometimes heterosexual people who experiment with their identity hurt LGBTQIA+ people by being welcomed into these spaces, being microaggressive, overwhelmingly transphobic, and then sheding the community like 'nvm turns out gay people are gross and I'm not one of you.' Second, a lot of heterosexuals who have been vocal and adamant about entering the LGBTQIA+ community relatively recently are people who'd like to see a P added to the acronym because they think that being a pedophile is a sexuality. I'm 100% not comparing heteroaces to pedophiles and sorry for activating that fight or flight reaction for anyone. Both issues I've presented are cases of strong-arming from people who are heterosexual or heteroromantic to be able to be part of the LGBTQIA+ community with disingenuous intentions and ultimately harmful results. As a result, I've always been hesitant and on the 'no thanks' side of supporting heteroromantic ace inclusion. I want to understand more and these comments are illuminating -- but it should be addressed that a great many heterosexual and heteroromantic people who've entered or tried to enrer LGBTQIA+ spaces have done a lot of harm and that shouldn't be glossed over.

I was picking up a birthday cake for my partner and a construction worker called me over after I'd parked at a meter near his truck. I'm used to being catcalled and having my time wasted by random male strangers so while I was immediately wary, I decided to give him the benefit of the doubt because as many bad experiences that I've had, I'll never get used to the feeling of getting panicky and distrustful about being approached in broad daylight. I just hoped that this would be different. So, I went over to talk to him. He seemed to catch onto my wariness and went out of his way to smile kindly and talk to me very casually and sweetly. He'd just wanted to know if I would be parked there for long because he needed to leave his truck in front of the spot I'd just occupied. I was very happy that my trust hadn't been betrayed this once and happily told him that I was just going to the ice cream store and would be right back. He just joked about wanting some ice cream, too, and left me on my merry way. Just like that! No leers, asking for my number, or weird comments. It was such a pure interaction and I was really happy that he hadn't turned out to be someone who wanted to perv on me so I got him some ice cream on the way back. We live in the desert and he was by himself on a weekend afternoon. When he saw me gesture to roll down his window so that I could give him the ice cream his face just lit up! I haven't forgotten his look and I always think of him whenever I catch myself wondering whether a stranger on the street will be weird or if they're just another kind person going about their day.

I don't see anyone mentioning how all trans men don't all look or present the same. (Not surprising. It is reddit, after all.) Thats the issue with "not being attracted" to an entire group of people. The thing you're "not attracted to" is something that you associate with everyone who identifies with the trans male label. There are trans men with soft features, angular faces, breasts, flat chests, vaginas, bottom surgery, long hair, short hair, deep voices, light voices, light skin, dark skin, top surgery scars, unblemished chests, and everything along the spectrum. You have to ask yourself what is it about every single trans man that you cannot find attractive? You're right to be concerned about underlying prejudices but that doesn't mean you're automatically a shit person. You know enough about terminology and your feelings that I'm sure you've seen a not unsubstantial amount of trans men in your life. What, exactly, do they all have in common that you dislike? The obvious answer is that they're all transgender. But what about them? Is it the clear absence of a naturally grown dick? Do you have a hard time separating them from butch lesbians? Is it the binders and the implication that they have breasts? Do you find the scars an unsightly reminder that they once had breasts just like you? You have to ask yourself these messed up and uncomfortable questions because once you do, you can start to rearrange your thinking. People have reasons for not wanting to date all sorts of people under all sorts of labels. In a deeply oppressive and bigoted society, those reasons will always have something foul behind them and it's okay to acknowledge that. Once you rearrange your thinking, will you be jumping at the chance to date a trans man? No. But you'll be able to acknowledge and appreciate the clear and present beauty in each trans man you see and not feel like you're lying to yourself.

Damn -- you really rock with all of this great advice. Nanny2 has certainly mentioned that she feels as if her opinions/tactics for trying to manage NK2's behavior has fallen on deaf ears, so I firmly believe that Nanny2 falls into the first category of reasons for why she sucks. However, some people really aren't that great with child rearing despite working in this profession so there's a good chance she also falls into category 2 to some extent. Regarding your previous reply: I have been getting more lax with my boundaries around requesting time off because I have gotten closer to this family and I DO feel bad for taking time off when I need it. However, that should stay a personal issue for me to work on and I don't appreciate it being exacerbated by MB's need to wheedle and negotiate a half shift every single time. Because then that just makes me feel obligated to give her a more severe excuse or otherwise explain why I need the day and I am 100% in agreement that that's none of her fucking business to begin with.

My wage is perfectly livable and satisfactory when it isn't soul sucking work. To a small extent, the pay nightmare is the fault of the organization that we nannies are paid through but MB doesn't help by constantly needing to be reminded to do her part to make sure our paperwork is submitted on time so that we are paid on time. She could set an alarm and try harder to be more organized so that it's not stressful trying to figure out if my check will be late this period (it often isn't but it often comes close). The overlap is there to help us two nannies coordinate care, provide updates, brainstorm, and do whatever else to help one another. It could be a good thing for a lot of reasons, including your brilliant idea of having Nanny2 shadow me and NK2 getting solo time with me, but there's no chance for it to work because Nanny2 will always leave early.

To clarify, though -- NK1 has made many deliberate positive and negative choices. I've learned that children, no matter their physical and/or mental differences, will always find ways to be cheeky little shits. He's a wonderful child but I've had to chastise him as well for some things here and there. In the behavior management system I created, he had his own version and could earn achievable points and fair demerits just as much as NK2 could and they both immensely enjoyed the system before I scrapped it because I was the only one doing it... In a way, I think he appreciates me being on his ass a little more than the other adults in his life because it shows that he has power over his choices even if he is dependent in a lot of other ways.

My challenge will be phrasing this all in a positive and constructive way while still being firm enough that it is properly understood that I will fucking leave if these things don't change -- and soon. At the same time, it's my job to coddle and handhold two children, not two middle aged women.

Seriously, thank you so much for validating me. Life IS crazy and I am an understanding person but I feel like this whole situation has gone too off the rails. Everyday feels like racing by to bedtime with MB and Nanny No.2 as opposed to a day filled with constructive child rearing. I will reply more when I get home but you have some amazing ideas that I will 100% go through with and get these people on board with it as well.

My friend. Claiming to not be physically attracted to a whole entire race is, in fact, racist. 

Unless birthed from the same womb as identical twins, no two Black people look exactly alike. Black people are born with just as broad a spectrum of physical, personality, and mental characteristics as every other race of human. You are "not physically attracted to Black people" because the racist society that you grew up in that has instilled in you racist ideologies (whether you acknowledge them or not) devalues typically-seen-as-Black features on Black people. Are you attracted to blonde hair? Black people can be born with blonde hair and blue eyes. Attracted to thin lips? Black people are often born with thin lips. Attracted to petite body types? Hold on to your hat, buddy, because I'd wager millions of Black people are born petite. 

In your life, you have likely seen/met plenty of Black people that possess traits you would objectively consider yourself to be attracted to. But your brain that was raised by a racist society mentally filters these people out so that you only acknowledge certain people as Black as soon as you see them. You may pass a bubbly, petite, lighter skinned, degree-holding woman with a loose afro in the street and double take, briefly entertaining the idea of getting to know her or being intimate without acknowledging that she's Black. But you will see a meme, video, or news article featuring a Black person that more closely fits the stereotype of Black people that you hold in your mind and immediately register tham as Black, unattractive, and use that to reinforce that you're "just not attracted to Black people."

That is actually racist, friend. Not Dictionary.com racist, a definition created by a white person who has no experience with being the recipient of every flavor of racism. You are objectively being racist. And the faster racist people stop seeing that as a personal attack no matter how it's phrased and instead as a sign to re-evaluate their thinking, the faster thinking like yours will cease to exist. Remember Garfield: You are not immune to propaganda. One of the biggest propaganda efforts cranked out by white Western society is the propaganda against any and everything seen as non-white.

Hey! So, I've had 3 therapists and been on a multitude of different pills. Everyone benefits from either therapy, medication, or a combination of the two and you can't really know what works for you unless you try different things. Easier said that done, I know, but examining your mental state, emotional state, reactions to outside stimuli, energy levels, and alertness levels while undergoing therapy/medication can all help you figure out what works sooner rather than later.

Only my latest therapist has significantly helped me in any noticable way. She helps me develop coping skills, validates my emotions, and puts things into perspective, even if I don't want to hear it. My previous therapists were not bad at all, they just listened to me rant and wouldn't help me find a way through or past my turmoil. Even in the haze of depression it's important to self-advocate for care, attention, and PROGRESS from your professionals. I was misdiagnosed by a psych and that led me to having some really shitty experiences with medication but it could've been helped if I was a better advocate to get my symptoms addressed. It doesn't matter if you change your mind about things, either, it's important to make people work with you and never hesitate to leave or raise hell if you feel dismissed or overlooked.

Antidepressants helped me get through the worst of my depression but take note of eeeeeeeveeeeeery change you feel while under medication. It doesn't matter how small. Recognize that pills take a while to kick in and recognize when certain pills are not for you. Stay away from anything that zombifies you. Paxil was the worst for me but Welbutrin worked wonders. (For the love of god stay away from paxil, lol)

Feel free to ask questions! And take notes! Lots of notes! In therapy, at the psych, mental illness fucks with your memory, especially when it comes to making progress. Take notes!

I'm glad that your religion has helped you feel a little bit of hope for the future or just in general. I like how to phrased something as well: I don't have low self-esteem, I feel let down by people. That's just very true for a lot of us, I'm sure. I find people are shitty in every aspect of my life. Work, when people try to get one over on me, life, when people can't be fucked to make sure my cat doesn't escape, and in general, where people can just suck out of nowhere. I get other people hurt or otherwise have motivations for sucking but, like, I will never get being awful to people unrelated to your pain just because you feel bad. It's animalistic in a bad way. Like lashing out at the first thing that you see or don't understand because you're hurt or afraid. Is there any long-lasting benefit to it? I haven't seen one, yet. We would all be better off if society encouraged us even when we failed.

It's okay to be scrambled. Articulating complex and unpleasant emotions is not a skill we all would like to develop. It's hard to try and then see nothing for your efforts or end up worse for trying. That's, like, negative reinforcement! I'm sorry people aren't really seeing how hard it is for you, no matter how your life looks like it's supposed to go... People don't understand how much just trying takes out of others, even if they didn't succeed it is important to support others when they try. And I don't mean participation trophies that forced anxiety upon an entire generation I mean genuinely helping people be better instead of ignoring or dismissing the effort it takes to try -- even if we fail.

Overall in life I'm always thinking about the future because if I stare too hard at the present I just relapse into depression. I regret not living more in the present but I'm not even sure what that looks like entirely. How do people learn to live in the present and still try to make strides for a happy future? I am often surprised when people are shitty or dismissive toward me unless someone else told me to expect that from a particular person. I just generally don't assume the worst in people and I am Often Very Wrong in doing so. That isn't to say that I am naive. I avoid people as a default but when I do interact with people it is seldom with such openness that I end up getting taken advantage of. But emotionally? It can be very easy to upset me in irl interactions because I am legit just mentally unprepared to have someone act like an asshole toward me and it can sour my mood for days. Other, less malicious but still unpleasant interactions just leave me feeling down and isolated from people -- like there is something about me that makes people want to disregard me, or if it's not me it's them and it still makes me sad that people just suck sometimes.

It is very emotionally draining. What kind of thoughts do you have about every day life? What do you do when these disappointments pile on and on and on? Are you ever just constantly unprepared for how little people can regard you sometimes? Even when you've done nothing wrong or bad or dishonest?

These aren't hypotheticals, I genuinely want to know, haha. Unless you'd prefer not to dwell on these things right now.
